current_project_basis.existing_alignment_direction: Measure matched-site CKA and orthogonal-Procrustes alignment, then compare native, unaligned cross-checkpoint and aligned cross-checkpoint steering bidirectionally with causal controls.
current_project_basis.new_gap: The existing direction correctly requires calibration-only Procrustes fit and held-out alignment, but no exact project contract was found that makes the fitted alignment transform itself a frozen evidence-bearing artifact with anti-leakage, no-post-hoc-selection and held-out causal-use rules.

deduplication.repository_search_at_observed_head: cross checkpoint Procrustes holdout leakage transform calibration crossfit alignment selection steering
deduplication.boundary: Search absence is not proof that no semantically related donor exists elsewhere. This artifact therefore adds only the narrow transform-governance discriminator and does not create a second J-Space authority or replace V51.

external_primary_method_inputs.source: Agarwal (2026), Cross-Architecture Steering Transfer in Language Models: A Systematic Empirical Study, arXiv:2608.05164
external_primary_method_inputs.finding: Cross-model representation alignment and steering transfer are conditional rather than guaranteed. The reported study finds stronger validated alignment and steering transfer at larger scales and weaker transfer in the smallest tested regime, making direct small-model coordinate portability unsafe to assume.
external_primary_method_inputs.project_implication: The approximately-0.8B Trigger-2 target requires exact checkpoint-pair/site/function validation; architecture equality and hidden-width equality cannot promote a shared raw-coordinate ABI.

external_primary_method_inputs.source: Cloos et al. (2024), Differentiable Optimization of Similarity Scores Between Models and Brains, arXiv:2407.07059
external_primary_method_inputs.finding: High representation-similarity scores need not imply matching task-relevant information or functional organization, and the interpretation of CKA/Procrustes-like similarity depends on the measure and dataset.
external_primary_method_inputs.project_implication: Geometric fit is only a descriptive prerequisite. Global J-Space/control credit requires held-out causal transfer and natural-consumer evidence, not a high alignment score alone.

external_primary_method_inputs.source: Achara et al. (2026), Multi-Way Representation Alignment, arXiv:2602.06205
external_primary_method_inputs.finding: Multi-model alignment may use a shared reference universe, but different alignment objectives favor different downstream properties; strict isometric alignment and retrieval-oriented agreement are not interchangeable.
external_primary_method_inputs.project_implication: Trigger-2 must declare what property an alignment transform is meant to preserve. A transform fitted for geometric agreement cannot silently be treated as a causal-control transform.

material_finding.finding: A learned cross-checkpoint transform can absorb idiosyncrasies of calibration prompts, sites, functions or intervention outcomes. If transform choice, hyperparameters, rank, site, sign, regularization, prompt family or donor direction is selected after seeing validation/holdout causal effects, then an apparently successful aligned steering result can contain evaluation leakage even when the downstream holdout rows themselves were never used in gradient-based model training.
material_finding.consequence: The alignment artifact needs its own provenance and freeze boundary. Coordinate alignment must be treated like a fitted metrology component, not a harmless visualization step.
material_finding.epistemic_boundary: This is a method-risk finding. No current Qwen3.5 alignment transform has been executed or shown to overfit by this artifact.

hypotheses.hypothesis: For some matched Qwen3.5 sites and process functions, checkpoint drift is approximately captured by one calibration-fitted orthogonal transform whose held-out geometric and causal-transfer performance remains stable.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The apparent alignment is calibration-family specific or function-specific and will collapse on sealed families, novel operations or reverse-direction transfer.
hypotheses.cheapest_future_discriminator: Fit exactly one preregistered transform on calibration activations only, freeze its digest, and evaluate untouched held-out prompt families plus bidirectional causal steering without refit.

hypotheses.hypothesis: High held-out CKA/Procrustes similarity predicts useful causal steering transfer at the declared site/function scope.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The aligned spaces share dominant geometry while task-causal directions or natural consumer paths differ; geometric similarity will therefore fail causal transfer or create off-target effects.
hypotheses.cheapest_future_discriminator: Compare geometric alignment against native, raw-cross, aligned-cross, shuffled-pair and random-orthogonal interventions at matched activation-scale/norm budgets.

hypotheses.hypothesis: One transform per checkpoint pair/site type is sufficient for the reusable process directions relevant to HCU.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Alignment is function-, layer-type- or carrier-specific; one global transform hides multiple incompatible local maps.
hypotheses.cheapest_future_discriminator: Predeclare global versus stratified transform classes, fit each only on the same calibration families under matched complexity, and compare sealed worst-family causal-transfer performance without post-hoc transform switching.

fit_boundary.rule: If any forbidden signal influences transform fitting or transform-family selection, the affected validation/holdout scope is contaminated and cannot mint alignment or checkpoint-selection credit.

artifact_freeze.law: Freeze the transform artifact and digest before opening validation/holdout causal results. Any refit creates a new transform identity and requires a still-sealed evaluation scope.

required_measurements: held-out geometric similarity on families never used for fit
held-out raw cross-checkpoint steering causal effect
held-out aligned cross-checkpoint steering causal effect
effect-size retention normalized by intervention norm and activation scale
worst-family and tail performance rather than mean only

crossfit_diagnostic.method: Optionally rotate family-disjoint calibration folds and fit one transform per training fold to estimate transform instability without consuming the final sealed holdout.
crossfit_diagnostic.use: Detect whether a seemingly good transform is highly dependent on the calibration family composition.
crossfit_diagnostic.restriction: Cross-fit results may diagnose instability but cannot be mined to choose a final transform after final-holdout unblinding.

promotion_semantics: Held-out causal transfer without frozen transform provenance => NO_DURABLE_ALIGNMENT_CREDIT.
Aligned transfer that beats raw transfer but fails off-target/locality controls => NO_PORTABLE_JSPACE_CONTROL_CREDIT.
A transform that works only for one process_function_id may be admitted only at that exact scope, not as global J-Space coordinate equivalence.
If a simpler identity/raw mapping performs equivalently under uncertainty, do not claim the learned transform is necessary.
Cross-checkpoint alignment cannot select a checkpoint winner by itself and cannot mint training, HCU or EntityOS runtime credit.

feedback: Do not teach raw hidden coordinates as checkpoint-invariant semantics.
Represent J-Space control references as checkpoint/site/function scoped objects with explicit optional alignment-transform identity.
Prefer function-level causal invariants over coordinate identity as the reusable HCU language boundary.
Keep renderer transportability, checkpoint identity, carrier causality and alignment-transform validity as separate gates; passing one cannot promote another.
